subject: Next steps: model-fit recommendations & prompt inventory for NovaCorp
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Sullivan <liam@novacorp.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps: model-fit recommendations & prompt inventory for NovaCorp

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call recap (high level):
- NovaCorp search team is evaluating a QA + rerank flow for customer-facing help articles and internal KB.
- Primary goals: precision at top-3, reduce hallucinations on sensitive legal content, and keep tail latency < 400ms under 95th percentile for web queries.
- Data constraints: cannot send raw customer PII; redaction required at ingestion.

Redwood recommendations (model fit):
- For initial eval: run Llama-2-Chat-70B-8k q4 and Mistral-Instruct-30B as candidates (we'll surface cost/latency tradeoffs in the benchmark link below).
- Add a smaller distilled candidate (Gemini-mini-equivalent) for latency-sensitive routes and reranking.
- Use our reranking pipeline with embeddings + pairwise rerank to maximize top-k precision.

What we need from you (prompt inventory & edge cases):
1) A prioritized list (10-25) of representative user prompts/search queries that should absolutely be covered in the evaluation (examples + expected/acceptable outputs where possible).
2) A separate file with known edge cases: PII-containing queries, ambiguous entity references, truncation scenarios, and examples that historically triggered hallucinations. Mark any items that are "must redact".
3) Indicate any regulatory redaction rules or specific token-level redaction policies (e.g., mask any 9+ digit sequences that look like SSNs, keep client IDs but strip names, etc.).

We've attached a prompt inventory template (prompt_inventory_template.csv) to make collection easier — please drop your sample prompts into that CSV. Also linking: our internal benchmark dashboard showing preliminary perf estimates for the model candidates: https://redwood-internal.company/benchmarks/nova-20260517 (read-only).

Next steps / timeline:
- You: fill and return the prompt inventory and edge-case file by EOD Tuesday (2026-05-19) if possible.
- Us: we will run an initial benchmark (latency & quality) within 48 hours of receiving prompts and share a short report + prioritized prompt failures.
- Joint: schedule a 30-minute follow-up to walk results and agree on canary routing (suggest Wed/Thu next week).

Attachments: prompt_inventory_template.csv (CSV), benchmark_summary_20260517.pdf (summary of candidate model profiles).

If you want, we can redact the CSV template for you (we can accept redacted samples).

Thanks — looking forward to the prompt set.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: prompt_inventory_template.csv]
From: Liam O'Sullivan <liam@novacorp.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Chen <maria@novacorp.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: model-fit recommendations & prompt inventory for NovaCorp

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. This lines up with our internal notes. A few quick answers and clarifications: 

- We'll aim to populate ~20 high-priority prompts and a short edge-case list by COB Tuesday. Maria (cc) will own gathering the internal examples.
- For redaction: we need to strip customer names and email addresses before sending anything external. We can keep internal IDs masked as CLIENT-XXXX. Can't share SSNs or full account numbers; if a prompt contains them we'll provide a redacted version and a private redaction mapping internally.
- One of our pain points: long-form queries where users paste full emails (often with signatures). We'll include 6-8 examples of those; please confirm how Redwood recommends handling signature/footer trimming in the prompt pipeline.

Two sample prompts to seed the template (also attached as quick text below):
1) "Help me find the contract clause about termination for convenience in the Acme service agreement."
2) "Customer pasted an email about their billing dispute — summarize action items and suggest next steps. (Includes name and partial account ID)"

We attached a small file with 5 raw examples to illustrate the format (nova_prompt_samples.txt). Let me know if you need us to do any pre-redaction before upload.

— Liam
Director, Search Engineering
NovaCorp
[Attachment: nova_prompt_samples.txt]

On Tue, May 18, 2026 at 09:12 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Liam —
> 
> Thanks again for the demo earlier...
From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: model-fit recommendations & prompt inventory for NovaCorp (internal)

Vanessa / Sean — quick internal note on evaluation concerns and measurement: 

- Quality/regression risk: given NovaCorp's legal/contract search use case, we should include hallucination-focused evals (precision@3 with hallucination penalty). I recommend adding an explicit hallucination flag in our eval CSV so reviewers can mark "asserted-but-unsupported" outputs.
- Redaction guidance: we should provide two ingestion modes in the template: (A) client-redacted inputs (what client will send), (B) server-side redaction expectations (what Redwood will apply before model). That makes testing end-to-end easier.
- For metrics: add a readability verdict and an actionability label for the "summarize and action" style prompts. Those are important success criteria for the customer.

Also, attach the benchmark summary (benchmark_summary_20260517.pdf) to the outbound follow-up and call out cost delta between the 70B and Mistral models so sales can set expectations.

I'll draft a short eval rubric we can send with the template (precision/recall/top-k/hallucination/actionability). If you want I can pre-populate 5 challenge prompts from our internal corpus to seed the comparison.

— Rachel
Product Manager, Evals
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Sullivan <liam@novacorp.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: model-fit recommendations & prompt inventory for NovaCorp

Liam — great, appreciate the quick turnaround. Final confirmation and links below: 

Action items (we'll take these once we receive your files):
- Redwood: run first-pass benchmarks (latency + quality + hallucination checks) on the candidate models and return a short report within 48 hours of receiving your completed template.
- NovaCorp: upload the completed prompt_inventory_template.csv and edge-case document (redacted as necessary) to the secure share link here: https://redwood-secure-share.com/upload/NC-2026-Q2-43 (or reply to this thread with attachments).
- Schedule: My calendar link for a 30-min results review: https://cal.com/vanessa/redwood (I blocked Wed/Thu next week 10:00-12:00 PT for this).

Notes on redaction & ingestion:
- Please send redacted samples if you have PII — we will not request raw SSNs/PII. Our ingestion pipeline will apply additional heuristics to strip obvious credentials and email addresses; please include examples you want preserved (like CLIENT-XXXX IDs) in the CSV.
- Signature trimming: we recommend a lightweight heuristic (strip content after a detected signature delimiter like "--" or "Thanks,") before tokenization; we'll include this in the eval so you can see impact on retrieval and summarization prompts.

Attachments included for your reference: prompt_inventory_template.csv, benchmark_summary_20260517.pdf.

If anything changes on timing, ping me and we can adjust the follow-up window.

Talk soon.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
